prompt: Who proposed removing the operator ID field from the data extract, who agreed, and had it already been sent anywhere by then?

answer.text:
Priya Nair (Acme IT Integration Lead) proposed removing the operator identifier field from the data extract. In the 24 September 2024 master data workshop she said "We do not need to send you... Then let us take it out" after Kwame Boateng flagged the unexpected operator identifier column on write-off records [, ]. Nadia Haddad (RELEX Solution Consultant) agreed on the receiving side, saying "I do not need to receive it" [], and Priya confirmed it as a five-minute change she would put on the list []. Ana Duarte noted it as an action []. The exclusion was later formalised as a condition by Priya in the 17 November 2025 go/no-go call [] and confirmed in writing by Nadia on 19 November 2025 []. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

On whether it had already been sent anywhere by then: yes. Kwame Boateng reported on 24 November 2025 that OP_ID was present in the raw landing zone for every daily file since 14 February and in the June and September reconciliation extracts for the data quality review; two of those were emailed as attachments, once to Priya and once to a distribution list of nine people including three at Meridian []. Priya had also stated in the go/no-go call that the field had been in every feed since February []. Kwame could purge the landing zone but not the emailed attachments []. [8] [9]

citations.quote:
Answer on the historic files.

OP_ID is present in the raw landing zone for every daily file since 14 February. It is
not carried into the aggregated waste tables, which group by store and article.

However it is present in the reconciliation extracts we produced in June and September
for the data quality review, because those were row level. Two of those were emailed as
attachments, once to Priya and once to a distribution list of nine people including
three at Meridian.

I can purge the landing zone. I cannot purge the attachments.
